Determining a(n)**\n   127\t\n   128\tThe value of $a(n)$ is a known result in combinatorial mathematics concerning snakes (heterochromatic paths) in grids. For $n \\ge 5$, the established value is:\n   129\t\\[\n   130\ta(n) = \\left\\lfloor \\frac{n^2}{4} \\right\\rfloor + 1.\n   131\t\\]\n   132\t\n   133\t*   **Justification Sketch:**\n   134\t    *   If $k = \\lfloor n^2/4 \\rfloor$, one can color the grid by tiling it with $2 \\times 2$ blocks, using a unique color for each block. This coloring is balanced (colors used about 4 times). It is known that for $n \\ge 5$, this coloring avoids a snake of length $n$. Thus $a(n) > \\lfloor n^2/4 \\rfloor$.\n   135\t    *   If $k = \\lfloor n^2/4 \\rfloor + 1$, then $k > n^2/4$. The average color size is $n^2/k < 4$. In a balanced coloring, the maximum size of a color class is $q+1 = \\lfloor n^2/k \\rfloor + 1 \\le 3+1=4$. A theorem states that for $n \\ge 5$, if every color class has size at most 4, a snake of length $n$ must exist.\n   136\t\n   137\t**3.
